original_title: Deep Learning-Guided Interface Engineering Stabilizes Oligomeric Enzymes
title: Deep learning redesigns an enzyme's interface for a 500-fold longer half-life
blurb: DeepIE uses deep learning to redesign the flexible regions where enzyme subunits meet, and on a dimeric formate dehydrogenase it rebuilt six interface regions into a variant with wild-type activity but roughly 500 times the half-life at 50°C. MD says it works by stiffening the interface and packing it tighter hydrophobically, a clean mechanistic story for a stability paper.

original_title: Tower Loop Engineering Converts a Low-Potential Bacterial Laccase into a High-Potential Laccase with Tunable Catalytic Activity
title: A "Tower loop" transplant turns a weak bacterial laccase into a strong one
blurb: Bacterial laccases run on a low-potential copper center that caps what they can oxidize, unlike their fungal cousins. Borrowing a fungal "Tower loop" into the small laccase from Streptomyces coelicolor, reworking the protein shell outside the usual copper coordination spheres, gets large, tunable jumps in that redox potential. A way to make a bacterial enzyme act fungal without swapping in the whole fungal enzyme.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Essential roles of lytic transglycosylases in l,d-transpeptidase-mediated peptidoglycan cross-linking in Escherichia coli.
title: Lytic transglycosylases turn out essential for E. coli's L,D cross-linking
blurb: E. coli builds a secondary set of peptidoglycan cross-links through L,D-transpeptidases, and this shows lytic transglycosylases are required partners for that cross-linking to happen at all.

original_title: A Sequence-to-Scaffold Platform Enables Programmable Carrier-Supported Biocatalysis for Nucleoside Analog Synthesis
title: An assembly line that goes straight from enzyme sequence to immobilized catalyst
blurb: SPACE pairs language-model-assisted mining of enzyme candidates with a scheme for loading the winners onto agarose-HPMC microsphere carriers, demonstrated here with nucleoside phosphorylases for nucleoside analog synthesis. The point is skipping the usual gap between finding a good enzyme and having a catalyst you can actually run a process on.

original_title: Exceptionally stable and safe lithium-ion batteries enabled by a unique electrolyte
title: A battery electrolyte that's liquid until it doesn't need to be
blurb: Sulfolane, LiTFSI, and a pinch of ultra-high-molecular-weight PEO make an electrolyte that shear-thins to soak into electrode pores while filling the cell, then thickens back up and stays put, cutting the leak and flammability risk of a normal liquid fill. They tested it in real 7-stack LFP|LTO pouch cells at heavy electrode loading rather than coin cells, which is further than most electrolyte papers bother going.

original_title: Long Fluorescence Lifetime Molecular Rotors Based on the 4,4‐Dicyano‐BODIPY Core
title: Swap two fluorines for cyanos and a viscosity probe suddenly lasts longer
blurb: Replacing the fluorines on a BODIPY molecular rotor with cyano groups slows non-radiative decay and stretches out the fluorescence lifetime, which matters for FLIM since a longer lifetime is what separates the probe's signal from cellular autofluorescence. It keeps the Förster-Hoffmann viscosity response intact, so the extra lifetime doesn't cost it sensitivity.

original_title: Janus Covalent Organic Framework Films With Macroscopic Directional Carrier Migration for Switchable Gas Sensing
title: A two-faced COF film that steers its own electrons
blurb: Fusing two lattice-matched COFs, COF-366 and its hydroxylated version, into one Janus film sets up a built-in electric field that pushes electrons and holes toward opposite faces instead of letting them diffuse randomly. They're using that directional charge separation to make the film's gas sensing switchable, and they call the sequence-controlled Janus construction a first for COFs.

original_title: Tailoring Local Anion Chemistry Affinity Enables Stable Halide–Sulfide Interfaces and Fast Ion Transport in Dual‐Electrolyte all‐Solid‐State Batteries
title: Getting halide and sulfide electrolytes to stop corroding each other
blurb: Halide/sulfide bilayer solid electrolytes pair an oxidation-stable halide with a reduction-stable sulfide, in theory, except the interface between them keeps degrading and strangling Li+ transport. Instead of slapping on a coating or buffer layer, this tunes the local anion chemistry so the two sides are intrinsically compatible, a cleaner fix if it actually holds up over cycling.

original_title: Tailored Polyoxometalates (POMs) For Next-Generation Energy, Catalysis, and Environmental Remediation: Structural Design, Mechanistic Insight, and Application Frontiers
title: The state of polyoxometalate tuning, in one review
blurb: A review rounding up how tailored POMs get engineered, lacunary defects, metal substitution, organic-inorganic hybridization, and what that tunability buys across energy, catalysis, and environmental cleanup. A field map, not a new result.
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

original_title: Engineering redox-active hyaluronan-ascorbate hydrogel microenvironments for β-cell protection during encapsulation and storage.
title: A hydrogel with its own antioxidant for storing encapsulated beta cells
blurb: A hyaluronan-ascorbate hydrogel engineered to be redox-active, built to protect encapsulated beta cells through the stress of encapsulation and storage.

original_title: Glutaredoxins Rapidly Reduce Glutathione Hydroper‐ and Polysulfides
title: Something finally reduces those glutathione polysulfides, and it's glutaredoxin
blurb: Hydropersulfides make handy radical-scavenging perthiyl radicals that self-recombine into polysulfides, but how those polysulfides get reduced back down was an open question. Stopped-flow kinetics and mass spec show a malaria parasite glutaredoxin, PfGrx, tears through glutathione trisulfide and tetrasulfide fast, filling in that step.

original_title: Bond Formation: Shaken, Not Stirred
title: Shaking the flask hard enough to make a bond form
blurb: Mechanical shaking, the thing everyone treated as just mixing, turns out to drive a regioselective intramolecular ether bond directly in water. They route that kinetic energy straight into Gibbs free energy to flip an sp2-to-sp3 hybridization at the core of a donor-acceptor system, and the process runs in reverse too. A strange new way to power bond formation that isn't heat, light, or a catalyst.

original_title: Phosphorene-Supported Rh Carbonyl Hydride Fragments as Efficient Heterogeneous Single-Site Catalysts for Ethylene Hydroformylation: A First-Principles Investigation
title: A computational case for hydroformylation catalysts you can actually filter out
blurb: Purely theoretical work: DFT plus microkinetics on HRh(CO)2 fragments sitting on black phosphorene, modeled as a heterogeneous single-site stand-in for the usual homogeneous Rh-phosphine catalysts that are a hassle to recover and keep intact. No bench data, just a first-principles argument that it should work.

original_title: Hidden Morphological Features in Organically Synthesized Porous Carbon Revealed through Analysis of Contradictory NMR Spectra
title: Solving OSPC's XPS-versus-NMR contradiction with morphology, not chemistry
blurb: XPS says this porous carbon battery anode material is built from sp and sp3 carbon, but the solid-state NMR spectra of both synthesis routes flatly didn't fit that picture. The fix isn't a different composition, it's a dense, heavily interpenetrated arrangement of that same sp/sp3 carbon, which is what was throwing the NMR off the whole time.

original_title: Facile Assembly of Functionalizable Conjugated Dienes via Skeletal Editing of Alkynyl Diazoketones Enabled by a Traceless 2‐Pyridyloxy Group
title: Diazoketones edited into stereodefined dienes, with the directing group erased afterward
blurb: Alkynyl diazoketones react with 2-pyridone-derived N,N-acetals under mild Lewis-acid conditions to build polysubstituted conjugated dienes with defined stereochemistry and a functional handle ready for further use. The 2-pyridyloxy group that makes the reaction work leaves no trace when it's done, which matters since stereodefined, heavily substituted dienes are normally miserable to make cleanly.

original_title: Single‐Particle FRET Probes Heterogeneity in the Ligand Shell of Colloidal Perovskite Quantum Dots
title: Watching the ligand shell on one quantum dot at a time, not the ensemble average
blurb: The inorganic core of a colloidal perovskite quantum dot can be mapped atom by atom, but the organic ligand shell around it has always been a soft, low-contrast blur. Tagging the ligand tails with dyes and reading single-particle photoluminescence lets them actually see how much that shell varies from dot to dot instead of settling for an ensemble average.

original_title: Circumventing Inner Filter Effects in Ultrafast Near-Infrared II (NIR-II) Up-Conversion Spectroscopy Using Front-Face Optical Configuration
title: A front-face fix for NIR-II fluorophores that keep absorbing their own signal
blurb: Self-absorption normally guts up-conversion ultrafast spectroscopy on near-infrared-II fluorophores, quietly eating the signal you're trying to measure. A front-face optical configuration shortens the path light travels through the sample, which suppresses that inner filter effect enough to record the real excited-state dynamics instead of an absorption-warped version of them.

original_title: Not all weights are made the same!
title: Not all weights are made the same!
blurb: Pictured first is an F1 grade 1g calibration weight from a very nice weight set that I use to calibrate my analytical balance (reads to 0.1mg), and the second picture is an (M1?) grade 1g weight from a ~$10 set off of Amazon. Just as a PSA to everyone to be careful when buying calibration weights. I didn’t know any better at first, and bought the $10 set when I first got the new balance, then quickly realized and bought the nicer set. Often you can find some really nice and high quality sets on eBay, however the calibration is usually out of date. Anyways, I suppose that’s sort of a digression

original_title: Standard protocol for aqueous soil extractions?
title: Standard protocol for aqueous soil extractions?
blurb: Hi my fellow environmental chemists, I am a mass spec guy who is in the uncomfortable position of having to develop a soil sampling and extraction protocol my collaborators can use to get me samples that I can do my mass spec on. I am totally good once my analytes are in water. But before that I am on the struggle bus Is there a standard somewhere that gives guidance on doing a water extraction from soil? We are doing a sort of simulated runoff study with some soil samples. I know what water I want to use, and like my storage conditions, but there is so much variety in the literature as far as

original_title: Transitioning from CA to NCA (177)Lu in the preparation of [(177)Lu]Lu-DOTATATE for PRRT - observations and considerations from a retrospective review.
title: What changes when DOTATATE prep switches to carrier-free Lu-177
blurb: A retrospective review of moving Lu-177 DOTATATE production from carrier-added to no-carrier-added material, weighing the practical snags that came with the switch.

original_title: Tyrosinase-Catalyzed Tyr–Aniline Coupling Enables Peptide Editing, Macrocyclization, and Phage-Display-Based Selection
title: One enzyme reaction for peptide labeling, cyclization, and phage display
blurb: Tyrosinase-catalyzed coupling of tyrosine to aniline groups, run in minutes under mild aqueous conditions, that the authors stretch into labeling, macrocyclization, and phage-display selection within a single reaction. Most Tyr-editing methods stop at labeling, so folding cyclization and ligand discovery into the same pot is the actual news here.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Benchmarking Automated Mass Photometry against SEC-MALS and AUC for Quantifying Cross-Linked Monoclonal Antibody Aggregates.
title: Mass photometry taking on SEC-MALS and AUC for antibody aggregates
blurb: Benchmarks automated mass photometry against SEC-MALS and analytical ultracentrifugation for quantifying cross-linked monoclonal antibody aggregates, the two techniques everyone already trusts for this. Worth watching if it can sub in for AUC's slower runs without losing accuracy.

original_title: High-yield on-resin synthesis of doubly crosslinked α-helical peptides with significantly improved protease resistance using an isophthalic acid-based crosslinker.
title: Doubly crosslinked helical peptides that shrug off proteases
blurb: An on-resin route to alpha-helical peptides stapled with two isophthalic acid crosslinkers instead of the usual one, made in high yield and holding up notably better against protease digestion.

original_title: Engineering cellular nitrene chemistry
title: Getting cells to run nitrene chemistry
blurb: Engineering cells to carry out nitrene-transfer reactions as part of their own chemistry, pushing biocatalysis into reactive-intermediate territory usually left to synthetic chemists on a bench.

original_title: WuXi XDC Achieves GMP Release for Singapore Bioconjugate Manufacturing Site - BioPharma APAC
title: WuXi XDC's Singapore bioconjugate site clears GMP
blurb: WuXi XDC's Singapore bioconjugate manufacturing site has gotten GMP release, adding another regulated production line for ADC-style work in Asia.

original_title: Programmable gold nanoparticle conjugates enable precise AMPA receptor localization at brain synapses by cryo-ET
title: Rigid gold nanoparticle tags pin down AMPA receptors in cryo-ET
blurb: Gold nanoparticles usually mark targets in cryo-ET through a flexible linker, which means the bead's position doesn't actually tell you where the target sits. Here the AuNPs attach directly to Fab fragments via cysteine residues instead, a rigid link that lets them localize AMPA receptors at synapses with real positional accuracy.

original_title: Lutetium-177 radiopharmaceuticals in cancer care: progress and challenges.
title: Where Lu-177 radiopharmaceuticals stand right now
blurb: A review of Lu-177 radiopharmaceuticals in cancer care, laying out the progress made so far and the challenges still in the way.

original_title: Tailoring the macromolecular architecture of covalently crosslinked xanthan gum/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogels for wastewater treatment: From nanometer mesh sieve to macroporous trap.
title: Dialing xanthan/PVA hydrogels from fine mesh to macroporous trap
blurb: Tuning the crosslink density of xanthan gum/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogels swings the pore architecture from a nanometer-scale sieve up to macroporous traps, built for wastewater treatment where different pore regimes catch different sized contaminants.

original_title: In vivo Quantitative Tomography of 225Ac Daughters in a Prostate Cancer Mouse Model with a Compton Camera
title: Tracking Ac-225's daughters in vivo with a Compton camera
blurb: Ac-225 alpha therapy looks promising in preclinical and clinical work, but imaging it is a mess: injected activities below 1 kBq/g, gamma branching ratios under 26%, and a decay chain that scatters signal across several daughters, all things SPECT struggles with. This group uses a Compton camera instead to get quantitative in vivo tomography of the Ac-225 daughters in a prostate cancer mouse model.

original_title: De novo design of protease-activatable cytokine prodrugs
title: Cytokines that only switch on where a protease says so
blurb: De novo designed protein prodrugs that stay masked until a disease-associated protease cuts them free, plus AND-gated split versions that need two separate cleavage events before the cytokine goes live. That two-key logic is the actual advance, tighter targeting than a single cleavage site can give you.

original_title: A Photoaffinity Probe for S‑Guanylation Posttranslational Modification to Identify Its Interacting Proteins.
title: A probe for catching S-guanylated proteins
blurb: A photoaffinity probe built to tag the S-guanylation mark and pull down whatever's interacting with it. Straight methods paper, no target list in what's given here.

original_title: How natural enzymes use noncanonical redox cofactors
title: Turns out enzymes already handle noncanonical redox cofactors fine
blurb: Biocatalysis with noncanonical redox cofactors has been stuck for lack of enzymes willing to touch them. This finds natural enzymes running NRCs at high rates, nails down the sequence motif responsible, and turns that into actual design rules for cofactor engineering. Nature already solved what people were trying to engineer around.

original_title: Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate Biosimilar Earns Final FDA Approval in GEP-NETs - CancerNetwork
title: A Lu-177 dotatate biosimilar clears the FDA
blurb: Final FDA approval for a biosimilar Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate in GEP-NETs, so the radioligand supply for these tumors stops being a single-vendor situation.

original_title: Assessment on site-specific thiol-based paramagnetic labeling strategies of metalloproteins for NMR and EPR applications.
title: Sorting out how to paramagnetically label metalloproteins
blurb: An assessment of site-specific thiol-based paramagnetic labeling strategies for metalloproteins, aimed at NMR and EPR work. Reads as a methods comparison rather than a new result.

original_title: Orthogonal Chemical Proteomic Strategies Reveal the Cholesteryl Ester Interactome in Mammalian Cells
title: Cholesteryl esters might not just be storage
blurb: Cholesteryl esters get treated as inert cholesterol stockpiles, but this chemical proteomics platform maps an actual CE-protein interactome using three separate photoaffinity strategies, metabolic probe incorporation, direct diazirine-alkyne delivery, and a fragment-based approach, checked against each other. If it holds up, the inert-storage story needs a rewrite.

original_title: Genetic Technologies for ADC Engineering - the-scientist.com
title: Genetic tools creeping into ADC design
blurb: A piece on using genetic engineering approaches for ADC construction. Just the headline here, no specifics to go on.

original_title: Spatiotemporal Control of Genetic and Epigenetic Editing through Covalent Tethering of CRISPR Nanoparticles to Zwitterionic Microgels
title: Tethering CRISPR nanoparticles to a gel instead of letting them drift
blurb: Non-viral CRISPR delivery usually means injecting nanoparticles and hoping, short-lived action, poor biodistribution. This covalently tethers them to zwitterionic microgels instead of relying on nonspecific adsorption, chasing delivery that's actually localized and sustained rather than aggregating off the scaffold.

original_title: Toward the Development of a Commercial Process to Produce Muvalaplin. Part II: Preparation of the Drug Substance
title: Scaling muvalaplin past the 100 kg mark
blurb: Process work on the Lp(a) inhibitor muvalaplin, reworking steps 5 through 7 for a 41% yield increase and 60% less process mass intensity versus the original discovery route, scaled safely beyond 100 kg. The unglamorous work of turning a discovery synthesis into something a plant can run.

original_title: An Efficient Platform for Enantioselective aza -Michael Addition to Both Linear and Cyclic Enones
title: One catalyst for aza-Michael addition on ring and chain enones alike
blurb: A bifunctional phase-transfer catalyst handles enantioselective aza-Michael addition across both linear and cyclic enones, 61 examples, up to 99% yield and 98% ee, spanning aryl, heteroaryl, alkyl, and ring-size variation. The adducts get carried into biologically relevant scaffolds, so this is pitched as a building-block method, not just a scope table.

original_title: Diastereodivergent Access to cis , cis - and cis , trans -Angular Triquinanes: Total Synthesis of (±)-Arnicenone
title: Two triquinane diastereomers, one starting material, one total synthesis of arnicenone
blurb: From the same allene precursor, a Lewis acid promoted intramolecular [3+2] Danheiser annulation delivers the cis,trans-fused angular triquinane, while a photochemical [2+2] cycloaddition followed by oxidative ring expansion gives the cis,cis isomer instead. Both routes converge on a total synthesis of (±)-arnicenone.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Labeling and Detection of Peptidoglycan in Chlamydia and Chlamydia-Related Organisms Utilizing D-Alanine Analogs.
title: Watching Chlamydia build its cell wall with D-alanine tags
blurb: A protocol chapter on labeling and detecting peptidoglycan in Chlamydia and related organisms using D-alanine analogs, for a genus whose cell wall has otherwise been a pain to see directly.

original_title: FDA Approves Bravnetsa, an Equivalent to Lutathera, for GEP-NETs - Cure Today
title: GEP-NET treatment gets a second option on the shelf
blurb: FDA approved Bravnetsa as an equivalent to Lutathera for GEP-NETs, meaning this radioligand therapy is no longer a one-drug market.

original_title: Enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of multi-helical nanographenes
title: Nanographenes with eight helicenes all twisted the same way
blurb: A modular stereoselective route controls the handedness of multiple helicene units within a single nanographene, reaching hexabenzocoronenes and graphene nanoribbons with up to eight uniformly aligned helicenes. The point isn't just the structure, it's that the chiroptical and near-infrared emission are tunable with it, aimed squarely at optoelectronics.

original_title: Photosensitizer-Free Synthesis of Arylsulfonated 4,5-Fused Polycyclic Coumarin Derivatives via Photoinduced Cascade Sulfonylation/Cyclization of 4-( N -Alkyl- N -acrylamido)coumarins
title: Coumarin ring-closing runs on visible light alone, no photosensitizer required
blurb: A cascade sulfonylation/cyclization of N-acrylamido coumarins with arylsulfonyl chlorides builds fused polycyclic coumarins at room temperature with no added photosensitizer, base, or oxidant. Broad substrate scope and a gram-scale run make the case that this isn't just a fussy small-scale trick.

original_title: Processing and Analyzing High-Throughput Microfluidic Enzymology Data: A Practical Guide To Rate Fitting and Quality Control
title: A field guide to not fooling yourself with enzyme kinetics data
blurb: A practical walkthrough of rate fitting and quality control for high-throughput microfluidic enzymology, covering how errors in image processing, initial-rate fitting, or kinetic modeling quietly propagate into the final numbers if nobody's checking. Aimed at anyone running HT-MEK or similar pipelines at scale.

original_title: Trifluoroallyl Sulfonium Salts: Reagents for Highly Regioselective Trifluoroallylation
title: A shelf-stable reagent for bolting a trifluoromethyl alkene onto your molecule
blurb: Trifluoroallyl sulfonium salts are bench-stable, scalable reagents that react with organozinc reagents under copper catalysis to give allylic trifluoromethyl-terminal alkenes with high regioselectivity. The authors also show the products carrying through further transformations, so it's not just a one-step party trick.

original_title: K2S-Mediated Tandem Selenylation and Cyclization of CaC2 with Diselenides: Synthesis of 2-Methylbenzoselenazole
title: Calcium carbide as your acetylene source for building benzoselenazoles
blurb: A one-step route to 2-methylbenzoselenazoles reacts diselenides with CaC2 as a solid acetylene surrogate, mediated by K2S. The mechanism is the actual news: K2S cleaves the Se–Se bond to generate selenium anions that form vinyl selenides, then a trisulfur radical anion from that same K2S activates the vinyl group for the ring closure.

original_title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Nitrile Hydration/Alkyne Hydroarylation Using 2-Cyano-Substituted Arylboronic Acids
title: One cobalt catalyst runs nitrile hydration and hydroarylation back to back
blurb: 2-Cyano arylboronic acids paired with 1-aryl-2-TMS-acetylenes go through a tandem cobalt-catalyzed nitrile hydration and regioselective alkyne hydroarylation to give 2-alkenyl primary benzamides in one pot, with chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity all landing where you'd want.

original_title: Divergent and Stereoselective Synthesis of Enamides via Visible Light-Driven Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer of Copper Catalyst
title: Copper's LMCT trick builds stereoselective enamides
blurb: A copper catalyst combines ligand-to-metal charge transfer with HAT and single-electron transfer to generate an acyl radical that forms the enamide and regenerates active Cu(II) in the same breath, keeping the cycle going. It's substrate-controlled, so chemo- and stereoselectivity shift with what you feed it, and functional group tolerance holds up.

original_title: Selective C18-Methyl Oxidation of Sclareol via an Engineered P450 Enables the Synthesis of Spiromyrrhene B
title: Directed evolution teaches a P450 to hit sclareol's stubborn methyl group
blurb: Primary methyl C-H bonds normally sit outside the reach of C-H oxidation chemistry without a directing group. Five rounds of evolving a P450BM3 variant took C18-methyl hydroxylation of sclareol from 4% regioselectivity to over 99%, with a better than twofold jump in activity too, and that opened a route straight to Spiromyrrhene B.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Construction of Tetrahydropyridobenzimidazoles via Ni–Al Bimetal-Catalyzed Tandem C(sp2)/C(sp3)–H Annulation
title: Nickel and aluminum team up to fully saturate a stubborn heterocycle
blurb: C-H annulation of benzimidazoles usually stalls at the (hydro)pyridobenzimidazole stage because the aliphatic C(sp3)-H bonds just won't react. A Ni-Al bimetallic catalyst pulls off tandem C(sp2)-H/C(sp3)-H annulation of N-alkyl benzimidazoles with alkynes instead, reaching the fully saturated tetrahydro-fused analogues in one pot.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Site-Selective C–H Arylation of Arenes: Using Diaryl Disulfides as an Arylation Reagent
title: A masked arylating reagent finally cracks meta-C-H on electron-poor arenes
blurb: Meta-C-H activation of electron-deficient arenes has been one of the stubborn holes in the toolkit. Diaryl disulfides work as masked arylating reagents under palladium catalysis and cover both electron-rich and electron-deficient arenes with the same method, which is the part that actually closes the gap.

original_title: Visible Light-Driven Chlorodifluoromethylation of Unactivated Alkenes
title: Cheap difluoroacetic acid turned into a radical alkene difluoromethylator
blurb: (Diacetoxyiodo)benzene and visible light convert difluoroacetic acid, about as unglamorous a reagent as it gets, into a CF2H radical that adds across terminal, di-, and trisubstituted alkenes and gets capped by NCS to finish the chlorodifluoromethylation. Good yields, and it runs on natural product substrates too.

original_title: Accelerated Green SN1 Reactions of the 9-Phenyl-9-fluorenyl Group
title: Shaking your way to a faster, greener SN1
blurb: Resonant acoustic mixing, essentially vigorous shaking, speeds up SN1 chemistry on the 9-phenyl-9-fluorenyl protecting group. PhF halides come straight from PhF-OH in concentrated acid, and PhF gets installed on amino esters like serine and hydroxyproline without protecting the alcohol side chain first, all in a friendlier solvent than the usual setup.

original_title: Stereoselective Polyglucuronic Acid Assembly via the Iron-Catalyzed Stereospecific Glycosylation with Glycal Epoxides
title: Iron catalysis makes glucuronic acid donors behave
blurb: Glucuronic acid donors are notoriously hard to activate, which is why stereoselective polyglucuronic acid synthesis has lagged. Iterative, stereospecific iron-catalyzed glycosylation with glycal epoxides strings together GlcA-β-1,4-GlcA linkages and reaches PGA octasaccharides with high stereoselectivity.

original_title: Functional Group Transpositional Trimolecular Cross-Coupling via Interrupted Homolytic Substitution
title: Nickel/photoredox reroutes allylamines into new isomers on demand
blurb: Constitutional isomers usually mean planning a fresh synthesis for each one. Interrupted homolytic substitution under nickel/photoredox dual catalysis redirects allylamine reactivity into a modular trimolecular cross-coupling instead, so a functional group can be repositioned rather than the whole route replanned.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Visible-Light-Promoted O-Glycosylation Mediated by Halogen Bonding of Selenoglycosides to the Diphenyliodonium Ion
title: Light plus halogen bonding gets glycosylation done at room temperature
blurb: Activating chalcogenoglycosides for O-glycosylation usually means strong electrophiles and cold reactions. Selenoglycosides and diphenyliodonium salts instead form halogen-bonded EDA complexes that visible light kicks into photoinduced electron transfer, giving high-yielding O-glycosylation at room temperature, with both experiment and computation backing the mechanism.

original_title: Unified Copper-Catalyzed Stereoselective Addition: Construction of Vicinal F/CF x -Containing Stereocenters
title: One copper catalyst covers the whole vicinal F/CFx stereocenter menu
blurb: A copper-catalyzed asymmetric Michael addition builds acyclic stereocenters sitting right next to a fluorine, whether the neighbor is CF3, CHF2, or CH2F, under one unified method instead of a separate recipe per flavor. Up to 20:1 dr and 98% ee, scaled up, with the DFT done on why the selectivity holds.

original_title: Self-S-sulfonation in a bacterial persulfide dioxygenase mediates thiol persulfide detoxification
title: A bacterial detox enzyme that sulfonates itself
blurb: A bacterial persulfide dioxygenase self-S-sulfonates as part of how it detoxifies thiol persulfides, a built-in step in its own cleanup mechanism.

original_title: Two-Step Design of Triazole-Stapled Opioid Agonists Exhibiting Potent and Prolonged Peripheral Analgesic Activity
title: A stapled opioid peptide built to stay out of the brain
blurb: Triazole stapling locks the peptide's shape, built in two steps: first tune the opioid pharmacophore into peptide 16, a mu-opioid agonist with better enzymatic stability and long peripheral analgesia, then bolt on an NPFF pharmacophore to get dual-target 16a. Peripheral-restricted opioid agonism is the actual pitch, less of the CNS baggage that comes with systemic opioids, assuming it holds up past the assays reported here.

original_title: Ligand-Free Eu(OTf)3-Enabled Photoactivation for Strain-Release Photocycloadditions of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with Substituted Alkenes
title: A cheap europium salt fills in for precious-metal photocatalysts on strained rings
blurb: Eu(OTf)3, off-the-shelf and ligand-free, coordinates bicyclobutane substrates directly so they absorb 420 nm light and pop into the 1,3-diradical without a separate photocatalyst. That diradical runs strain-release cycloadditions with electron-poor and aryl alkenes and annulates with vinyl azides, and they back it with gram-scale synthesis and a sonidegib bioisostere, so it's not just a curiosity reaction.

original_title: Ligand Engineering Controls Near-Infrared Emission, Quantum Efficiency, and Photoluminescence Lifetimes in Dimetallic Ru(II) Complexes
title: Tuning Ru(II) NIR emitters turns out to be less modular than you'd hope
blurb: Six ligands, six dimetallic Ru(II) complexes, varying methyl substituents, ring nitrogen count, and meta vs. para phenylene bridges to see what controls near-IR emission, quantum efficiency, and lifetime. The structural knobs don't turn independently, so tuning one property drags the others along instead of giving a clean dial for each.

original_title: Biocatalytic Redox Cascade Enabled Site-Selective Direct β-Alkylation of Cyclopentanones
title: Getting alkyl groups onto a ketone's beta carbon instead of the usual alpha spot
blurb: Direct beta-C(sp3)-H alkylation of cyclopentanones is normally out of reach, existing methods only touch the alpha or ipso positions. A photobiocatalytic redox cascade gets there with site selectivity even on alpha-aryl or alkyl substituted rings, a combination current catalysts reportedly can't manage.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Solution‐Processable Dicycloheptatrienerubicenes With Two Trialkylsilylethynyl Groups
title: Making a non-benzenoid PAH actually dissolve
blurb: Their dicycloheptatrienerubicene scaffold gets a bromination/borylation/oxidation/alkynylation sequence to install trialkylsilylethynyl groups at the 2,2' positions. The resulting TES and TIPS versions are solution-processable, and swapping the silyl group changes how the molecules pack in the solid state, a standard lever but a useful one on a scaffold this unusual.

original_title: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
title: Doping rhenium into an iridate so the iridium stops overoxidizing
blurb: Re-doped SrZrxIr1-xO3 hits a 250 mV overpotential at 10 mA/cm2 in acid with Ir mass activity above 1,300 A/g and keeps it up over time. The trick is that high-valent Re stabilizes a low-valent Ir active site and blocks the overoxidation that usually kills Ir OER catalysts in acid, meaning less of the expensive metal needed per amp.

original_title: Regulating Metal–Support Interaction via WO 3 Crystal Phase Engineering for Enhanced Acidic Water Oxidation
title: Picking the right WO3 crystal phase so single-atom Ir catalysts don't fall apart
blurb: Three WO3 phases, monoclinic, orthorhombic, tetragonal, give three levels of lattice distortion, and more distortion boosts the Ir single atoms' activity but wrecks their stability. Orthorhombic lands the best balance, the real point being that metal-support interaction strength is tunable by crystal phase alone, not just composition.

original_title: Self-recycling Fenton chemistry through the ordered hydration shells of Fe
title: Getting Fe3+ to regenerate itself in Fenton chemistry, no photocatalyst added
blurb: The usual Fenton bottleneck is Fe3+ sitting around waiting to be reduced back to Fe2+, which is why you dose in excess iron and end up with sludge. Here, ordering water molecules beyond Fe3+'s first coordination shell turns the whole hydration network into a visible-to-red-light antenna that shuttles electrons in and reduces Fe3+ back to Fe2+ on its own.

original_title: Theranostics in the management of prostate cancer: from concept to clinical practice.
title: A review of prostate cancer theranostics, concept to clinic
blurb: A review tracking prostate cancer theranostics from early concept work through to actual clinical use, no new data of its own, just a survey of where the field stands.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Defluorinative Alkylation for Accessing Cyclic Acetal– gem -Difluoroalkenes
title: Iron catalysis stitches cyclic acetals onto gem-difluoroalkenes
blurb: An Fe-catalyzed reductive defluorinative coupling between trifluoromethyl alkenes and dioxolanyl or dioxepanyl alkyl iodides trades one fluorine for a new C-C bond, building five- or seven-membered cyclic acetals fused right onto gem-difluoroalkenes in one step. Both motifs are already med-chem staples on their own, this just gets them built together instead of pieced in separately.

original_title: Pd-Catalyzed Skeletal Remodeling of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane Carboxamides to Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-ones via a Pd(II)–Carbene Intermediate
title: Turning strained bicyclobutane amides into azabicyclic scaffolds, via a transient Pd carbene
blurb: A Pd(II)-carbene forms in situ and drives skeletal remodeling of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane carboxamides straight to 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexan-2-ones, with an allyl handle left on for further elaboration. Good functional group tolerance across a structurally diverse scope, and the authors say the protocol scales, so this reads like a real method rather than a proof of concept.

original_title: Diboron‐Embedded Heteroacenes With Systematically Varied Central π‐Skeletons and Fusion Modes
title: Diboron heteroacenes where fusion mode, not core size, runs the show
blurb: Six diboron-embedded heteroacenes built off benzene, thienothiophene, or dithienothiophene cores via one-pot cyclative borylation. Absorption, emission, and the stepwise reduction behavior all track fusion mode rather than how big the π-core is, and crystal packing comes down to molecular symmetry instead of either. A tidy structure-property map, if a narrow one.

original_title: Bidirectional Alkene-Nucleophile Coupling at a Single Carbon Center Enabled by a Methylene-Bridged Thianthrenium Dication
title: Coupling an alkene and a nucleophile across a single carbon
blurb: Synthetic building blocks skew toward whatever biosynthesis happens to make, so hitting a target that differs by exactly one carbon from what's available can be disproportionately hard. A methylene-bridged thianthrenium dication lets an alkene and a nucleophile get coupled bidirectionally across that one carbon, filling the gap directly instead of hunting for the right precursor.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Borane-Catalyzed Divergent Hydrogenative and Silylative Reduction of Quinolinium Salts
title: One borane catalyst, two different quinolinium reductions, pick your solvent
blurb: B(C6F5)3 reduces quinolinium salts either way: dioxane gives the silylative product, dichloroethane gives straight hydrogenation, both in good to high yield. Both routes run through the same enamine intermediate, and the split seems to come down to how stable the silylium cation is in each solvent.

original_title: Design Principles to Promote Acid–Base Interactions with a Weak Second-Sphere Lewis Acid
title: Getting more out of BPin's weak Lewis acidity by shortening the leash
blurb: BPin is a weak Lewis acid on its own, but tethering it to an NHC scaffold and pulling in the tether improves preorganization enough to get cooperative substrate binding alongside the metal center. Experiment and computation both land on the same design lesson: keep the second-sphere acid close.

original_title: Methods for assessing binding of a small-molecule radioligand to soluble enzyme isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 variants
title: Working out how to actually measure a radiotracer binding mutant IDH1
blurb: IDH1 mutations in glioma make the enzyme churn out the oncometabolite 2-HG, and mutant-selective inhibitors are now being turned into radiolabeled tracers. This is the assay side of that story: methods for checking how a small-molecule radioligand actually binds soluble IDH1 variants, the unglamorous groundwork that has to exist before anyone trusts the imaging data.

original_title: Decoupled EDA Activation of Aryl Halides Enables Metal‐Free C–H Arylation of Pyrroles
title: Splitting the electron donor from the coupling partner in EDA-complex arylation
blurb: Usual EDA-complex chemistry makes the electron donor double as the nucleophile, which caps how modular it can be. Here N,N-dimethylaniline just donates the electron, forming a charge-transfer complex with the aryl halide under visible light while something else handles the coupling, arylating pyrroles with no photocatalyst and no metal.

original_title: Visible Light-Mediated Dearomative Remote Functionalization of Arenes via a Tandem Strain-Release Spirocyclization Relay
title: Dearomatizing arenes at a distance with a strain-release relay
blurb: BCB strain-release chemistry has already built lactams and indolinones off alkene and arene appendages, but dearomative functionalization of the arene itself hadn't been done. This gets there photocatalyst-free under visible light, using nitrosamines to install sulfonamides and oximes at a remove from the ring being opened.

original_title: Temperature and reproducibility in photocatalysis
title: Photoredox papers keep not reproducing, and here's why
blurb: A look at why photocatalysis results are all over the map from lab to lab: light source, temperature control, and co-catalyst use routinely go unreported or underspecified. Not a new reaction, just someone pointing out that half the field's methods sections aren't actually methods sections.

original_title: Synthesis of α-Halophosphonates via Copper-Catalyzed Atom Transfer Radical Addition
title: Cu-catalyzed ATRA gets you α-halophosphonates without babysitting the catalyst
blurb: Alkyl halides add across alkenylphosphonates under copper ATRA catalysis, with the radical initiator ACHN doubling as an in situ reductant that keeps regenerating Cu(I), so turnover stays high. Broad scope on the radical precursor side, for a class of building blocks pharma and agrochem both lean on.

original_title: Nonplanar S-Shaped Bisanthene: Synthesis, Structures, and Properties
title: An S-shaped, non-planar bisanthene that lights up when you charge it
blurb: A spiro-fused, doubly [4]helicene bisanthene made via cationic-radical C–H amination, stacking tightly in the solid state with a respectable 28% photoluminescence quantum yield as a powder. The redox states are reversible and absorb in the near-IR, which is the part that matters: it's a candidate NIR electrochromic material, not just a new shape to admire.

original_title: Modular Synthesis of Di‐ and Triazadibenzoazulenes by a Cross‐Coupling/Cycloisomerization Strategy
title: Two cross-couplings and an acid wash build the azadibenzoazulene core
blurb: Sonogashira then Suzuki-Miyaura, run in a chosen order, funnel into distinct regioisomers that a Brønsted acid then cyclizes into fused seven-membered diaza- and triazadibenzoazulenes. The trick is entirely in the coupling sequence, not the cyclization step.

original_title: Protonation-Gated Strain-Release Generation of Amino- o -quinodimethanes
title: A proton switch that turns ring-strain reactivity on and off
blurb: Amino-benzocyclobutenes only pop open into the reactive amino-o-quinodimethane once you strip the nitrogen lone pair's stabilization of the C-C bond, and protonating it shifts the barrier by more than 50 kJ/mol. That's a better than 1000-fold swing in reactivity from adding or removing a single proton, and the computed barriers actually match what they measured.

original_title: Visible-Light-Catalyzed In Situ Generation of Nitrile Oxides from Aryl Trichloromethane and TBN for [3 + 2] Cycloaddition to Access Isoxazoline/Isoxazole Scaffolds
title: Nitrile oxides made with light instead of a metal catalyst
blurb: Aryl trichloromethane, an alkene, and TBN under visible light generate the nitrile oxide in situ and cycloadd straight to isoxazolines, skipping the usual presynthesized dipoles or transition-metal catalysts. Mechanistic work pins PhCHCl2 as the actual intermediate along the way.

original_title: Synthesis of Benzylic Quaternary Centers via Arylation with Aryl(TMP)iodonium Salts
title: Quaternary benzylic carbons, courtesy of a hypervalent iodine reagent
blurb: Diaryliodonium salts arylate tertiary malonates to build benzylic quaternary centers, a transformation that's been oddly underdeveloped. DoE found mild conditions that tolerate even electron-rich arenes, and the iodonium synthesis telescopes with the coupling into one pot.

original_title: Alkoxyethyl Acetate Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
title: A fluorinated ether-ester electrolyte for 4.5V lithium metal cells
blurb: Bolting a carbonyl and a CF3 group onto a glycol-ether backbone gives TFE-EA, a solvent that breaks the usual symmetric bidentate solvation of ether electrolytes. Used as the main solvent in a LiFSI/FEC mix, it's built to keep both a lithium anode and an NMC811 cathode happy up at 4.5V.

original_title: Isoindole-Based Multicomponent Synthesis of Pyrimido[6,1,2- cd ]pyrrolizine Fluorophores with Unsymmetrical Urea Handles: Photophysical, Theoretical, and Antifungal Imaging Studies
title: One-pot fluorophores that also work as antifungal imaging probes
blurb: A multicomponent route builds a library of pyrimido[6,1,2-cd]pyrrolizine dyes carrying unsymmetrical urea groups, glowing orange-red in solution. Swapping side chains pushes the solid-state emission further red, and they've tested the things as actual antifungal imaging probes, not just photophysics on paper.

original_title: Dipyrrin-Strapped NiII Porphyrins
title: Strapping a dipyrrin onto a nickel porphyrin, then swapping in boron
blurb: A dipyrrin-strapped NiII porphyrin and its anthracene-bridged dimer are the first free-base carbasubporphyrin-fused porphyrins, built by Suzuki coupling. Treating them with BPhCl2/TEA converts the strap over to BIII carbasubporphyrin complexes, and the same coupling works with a fluorenyl partner too.

original_title: Programming Interfacial Function through Alternating Sequence in Amphiphilic Copolymers
title: Forcing amphiphilic copolymers to alternate on command
blurb: A bulky-monomer trick extends alternating copolymerization, so far mostly a vinyl-polymer party trick, to methacrylamide-acrylate systems, giving cationic alternating copolymers with real sequence control. The point being made is that spatial organization along the chain, not just overall composition, is what sets interfacial behavior.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Direct C1–H Amination of Free NH Carbazoles Enabled by the Catellani Reaction
title: Aminating carbazoles at C1 without touching the NH
blurb: A Pd/NBE Catellani reaction installs cyclic amines directly at C1 of free NH carbazoles, a position that's been hard to functionalize without multistep routes or nastier metals. Acyl, pivaloyl, and halogen substituents all survive, and it's apparently the first time the Catellani reaction has been extended to direct amination of unprotected carbazoles.

original_title: Enantioselective Defluorinative C(sp2)–H Allylation of Acrylamides Enabled by CpxRh(III) Catalysis
title: A rhodium catalyst pulls chiral fluoroalkenes out of ordinary acrylamides
blurb: Chiral fluoroalkenes are annoying to make asymmetrically, so this pairs asymmetric alkenyl C(sp2)–H activation with a defluorinative coupling step, using a chiral CpxRh(III) catalyst to run what's essentially an olefin-olefin cross-coupling. Out the other end: enantioselective, fluorinated skipped 1,4-dienes built straight from cheap acrylamides.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Secondary-sphere hydrogen bonding promotes catalytic nitrate reduction at iron
title: Hydrogen bonds do the binding an iron site can't manage alone
blurb: Nitrate barely sticks to metals and its N–O bonds don't want to break, which is why it's such a pain for molecular catalysts. Wrapping an iron complex in a network of secondary-sphere hydrogen bonds fixes the binding problem and pushes catalytic reduction all the way through to NO and ammonia.

original_title: Novartis secures new radioligand in $900M deal as competition strengthens
title: Novartis pays $900M for a radiopharma asset that's still preclinical
blurb: Novartis licenses a preclinical radioligand therapy from a Chinese biotech for up to $900M, a pipeline top-up as new radiopharma rivals start crowding the space. Preclinical means it's a bet on where the field's heading, not a near-term drug.

original_title: Reversing Benzene Bioisosterism through Photocatalytically Divergent Double Strain-Release Skeletal Remodeling
title: Running the flat-to-3D bioisostere trick backwards
blurb: The usual move is swapping planar aromatic rings for 3D bicyclo[1.1.0]butane bioisosteres. This photocatalytic method reverses it, unfolding BCBs back into highly substituted benzenes via a double strain-release step, and tuning the photocatalyst toward one pathway or another decides which product comes out. So the link between the flat and 3D chemical worlds runs both directions now.

original_title: O-mannosylation of fibrocystin and fibrocystin-L expands TMEM260 sequon selectivity and provides a potential link to the renal and auditory phenotypes of SHDRA
title: TMEM260 turns out to mannosylate fibrocystin too, which might explain SHDRA's kidney and ear symptoms
blurb: TMEM260 O-mannosylates IPT domains in the ER, and adding fibrocystin and fibrocystin-L (the PKHD1/PKHD1L1 proteins) to its substrate list stretches its known sequon selectivity further than expected. Fibrocystin mutations already cause kidney disease, so this gives a plausible mechanistic thread connecting O-mannosylation to the renal and auditory phenotypes seen in SHDRA.

original_title: Multimodal Sensitivity Enhancement of Binding-based Diagnostic Assays Using Functional Hydrogels
title: Swapping flat immunoassay surfaces for hydrogels without losing the signal
blurb: Standard immunoassays stick capture molecules onto flat surfaces, which caps loading capacity and tends to denature protein in the process. This is a general scheme for building hydrogels into immunoassay platforms instead, using bio-orthogonal chemistry to keep analytes getting through while boosting both optical and electronic readouts. They call it universal; worth seeing it survive someone else's assay first.

original_title: Nonalternating Chain Walking Polymerization Enables In-Chain Ketone Polyolefin Elastomers
title: A nickel catalyst that stops chain-walking and CO insertion from fighting each other
blurb: Branched polyethylene from packaging and ag film piles up as waste, and building ketones into the backbone to fix that has been blocked because nonalternating monomer insertion and chain walking are kinetically at odds. An asymmetric α-imino-ketone nickel catalyst with axial shielding gets the two to cooperate, yielding high-molecular-weight polyolefin elastomers with ketones built right into the chain.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: De novo synthesis of threofuranoses via a triple-carbonylation cascade of aldehydes
title: Threofuranoses in one pot, no protecting groups required
blurb: Building stereochemically complex sugar mimics is normally a protecting-group slog across many steps. A rhodium-catalyzed cascade that runs three carbonylations in sequence skips that entirely, turning plain aldehydes and CO straight into functionalized, oxygen-rich threofuranose scaffolds in one step.

original_title: DNA Nanotechnology Meets Peptide and Protein Self‐Assembly
title: DNA origami as scaffolding for peptides that want to self-assemble anyway
blurb: A review on pairing DNA's programmable base-pairing with peptides' and proteins' own tendency to fold into ordered superstructures, treating DNA nanostructures, origami especially, as a modular scaffold for hybrid DNA-peptide-protein materials. It's a survey, so the payoff is seeing the field mapped in one place rather than a new result.

original_title: Room Temperature Structures of Solvated Organic Molecules Enabled by Liquid Cell Electron Diffraction
title: MicroED learns to look at crystals still sitting in their own solvent
blurb: MicroED normally wants dry microcrystals because vacuum and radiation damage make solution-phase imaging hard. This traps a thin liquid film between two pressed carbon grids instead, getting room-temperature electron diffraction on organic microcrystals still suspended in solution. A hardware fix for what's mostly been a hardware limitation.

original_title: Intrinsic chain-end stabilization enables chain-transfer-agent-free living cationic ring-opening polymerization of cyclic enol ethers
title: Living polymerization that doesn't need a chain-transfer agent
blurb: Cyclic enol ethers polymerized cationically in living fashion, with the growing chain end stabilizing itself instead of relying on an external chain-transfer agent to keep the chains alive. One less reagent to babysit, assuming the molecular weight control holds up beyond the model monomers.
